newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB lowers Egis earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: CSFB lowers Egis earnings forecast.

text.p: CS First Boston (CSFB) on Tuesday lowered its earnings forecast for Hungarian drug company Egis for 1997 and 1998, but left its rating unchanged at "buy."
The revision follows an agreement between the Hungarian Association of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Hungary's social security authority over drug price increases next year.
"Drug prices are set to rise between nine to 11 percent next year, or five to seven percentage points lower than our expectations," CSFB's analyst Spencer Jakab said in a note to investors. @
On average, CSFB expects the real nominal increase in Egis drug prices to be closer to 13 to 13.5 percent, he said.
"This decision is bad news for Egis and we have lowered our 1997 and 1998 earnings forecasts in line with the change in pricing expectations," Jakab said.
"Egis will be relatively harder hit by the relatively low price increases than (other drugs company) Richter due to its heavier exposure to the domestic market," he said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Egis closed at 9,500 forints, down 100.
